rows.grounds: fused form: jīvan (present participle, √jīv) + eva (indecl.) + athavā (indecl.); sandhi fusion kept as one token
optative expressing prescribed or possible action
object of kuryāt; the individual self as recipient of the act
compound/resultative: śiva + saṃjñita (named, designated); describes the state made of oneself

items.question: Can a person consecrate himself as designated Śiva while still living?
premises: A ritual act of consecration can be directed toward oneself.
Such consecration may be performed while one is still alive.
The intended result is making oneself designated as Śiva.
items.inference: Therefore, even while living, a person may make himself designated as Śiva.
uncertainties: The exact ritual referent of making oneself śivasaṃjñita depends on the preceding context.
items.plain_english: Or else, while still living, he should make himself designated as Śiva.
